findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract, so building it raises TypeError.
findings.body: `StatefulDetectorHandler` has abstract methods (`get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, `counter_names` and the new `build_occurrence_and_event_data`), and this subclass only has `pass`. Before this change the handler's `evaluate` returned `[]`. Now, when `Detector.detector_handler` creates the handler for a `metric_alert_fire` detector, Python raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class`. That exception aborts `process_detectors` for every detector in the batch. I couldn't see whether `MetricAlertFire.detector_handler` points at this class, but the comment above it suggests it does. Either keep a working stub that returns `{}` until the stateful version is written, or implement the abstract methods.
